title: Stable and Carriage Shed — Yasnaya Polyana
visualBrief: Complete independent long stable/carriage building: plaster shell, pale plinth, green hipped standing-seam roof, three seated ridge vents, real recessed stall/window/door apertures, separate wide double carriage door and supported threshold aprons. Use shared stucco, stone_limestone, metal_standing_seam, wood_plain and storefront surfaces. Hidden rear details and exact roof/threshold layout are approximate; terrain grade adaptation remains draft until inspected.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Inferred from two ordinary museum stable/courtyard photos, the museum visitor-map stable marker, and the separate long rectangular footprint southeast of the three already owned Volkonsky footprints. Retained PMTiles does not label this building by name; keep this inference explicit. Exact retained way167382250 supplies the67.28x9.04m footprint and native axes; local negativeZ faces the inferred Volkonsky courtyard. No other Volkonsky building is owned. Front/rear assignment, opening census, roof vents and heights are photo-led approximations.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: One-story photo-led white plaster stable and carriage shed: wall3.05m above local floor, hipped green metal roof2.2m above eave, three ridge vents, four stable doors, wider3.7m carriage opening and high stall windows. Coarse native front-corner levels differ 3.296m over67.28m. This draft applies a 0.04899 long-axis grade to the floor/roof to fit retained terrain; this is an explicit terrain adaptation, not surveyed historical building geometry. Inspected native front/rear/threshold views retain the one-story silhouette and seat the plinth/thresholds. The mild long-axis floor/roof grade remains an approximation from coarse terrain, not surveyed historical construction.
